## b16 · 2026-09-08 — Starter deck summary: resolved as N/A

The one item left over from the class-select/map TODO sweep earlier today that needed
a product decision rather than more source-diving: whether a condensed inline "starter
deck summary" adds anything beyond the existing "STARTING DECK" → `DeckViewer` full
view.

Checked `CreateGameData.cs` before deciding rather than guessing: all 8 classes ship an
identically-shaped 10-card deck — always 6 class spells (2×/2×/1×/1×) plus the same 4
fixed neutrals (`focus`, `guard`, `amplify`, `mana_petal`). A composition summary (card
count, class/neutral split, etc.) would show the same numbers for every class, so it
couldn't help anyone compare or choose — it'd be decoration, not information. The real
differentiator, *which* 6 spells, is already surfaced by the signature-spell preview and
the full deck viewer. No UI change made; closed the checklist item in
`docs/wizard-select-todo.md` as resolved-N/A with this reasoning inline.

## b16 · 2026-09-08 — Clearing the remaining class-select and map TODOs

Worked through most of what was left unchecked in `TODO-map-uxui.md` and
`docs/wizard-select-todo.md` after the accessibility pass — everything that was
implementable from source without a device, live playtesters, new art assets, or a
product decision only Jared can make. Per-item scoping notes (including three real
risk catches made along the way) are inline in both TODO files next to each item;
this entry is the roundup.

**Explicitly out of scope for this pass, left untouched:** the "Optional Structural
Refactors" section of `wizard-select-todo.md` (Two-Panel desktop layout, Expandable
Rows, Dynamic Hero Section) — asked first, user said skip; five live-playtesting
items in `TODO-map-uxui.md` (route-planning speed, node recognition, etc.) — need
real players, not code; anything needing new icon/art assets or source art
regeneration; anything needing a physical device in hand; screen-reader labels —
genuinely new UI Toolkit accessibility infrastructure, not attempted blind.

### Class Select screen

- **Elevation shadow** on the selected roster card — added as the card's own first
  child (absolutely positioned, bleeding a few px past its edges), not a wrapper
  around it. `.cs-card` sets no `overflow: hidden`, so this needed no restructuring
  of the roster's tightly-tuned Phase-3 vertical-compression grid at all — the
  originally-deferred wrapper approach would have needed every one of that grid's
  ~15 breakpoint overrides mirrored onto a new host element.
- **Keyboard focus.** Roster cards are plain `VisualElement`s, so they needed
  `focusable = true` + `tabIndex` + an Enter/Space handler added explicitly; the CTA
  buttons were already natively focusable and only needed a `:focus` USS rule. Uses
  translate + opacity for related motion elsewhere in this pass, never scale, since
  `.map-node.available:hover` and `.cs-card` both already lean on real USS scale
  transitions that an inline scale write would clobber.
- **Roster comparison indicator.** A ★ badge on whichever stat(s) a class holds the
  roster max for (ties included) — one feature satisfying both "archetype comparison
  indicators" and "comparative guidance," which asked for the same thing from two
  different sections of the TODO doc.
- **Stat profile framing.** A small pill ("Offense-Focused", "Well-Rounded", ...)
  computed purely from the three power-axis stats already on screen — no invented
  balance claims, just a description of the numbers.
- **World flavor line.** One line per class, pulled verbatim from
  `jaredluyster.com/docs/Bibles/world-and-lore.md`'s "Wizard Classes — Flavor Notes"
  table (e.g. Pyromancer: "Woke up setting things on fire. Learned to aim.") — Jared's
  own existing copy, not written for this pass.
- **Signature spell preview**, rendered via the existing `CardView.BuildSpellCard`
  rescaled through `CardViewOptions` rather than a bespoke layout, so it stays in
  sync with any future card-visual change automatically. 7 of 8 picks are quoted
  directly from `classes.md`, which names each class's "defining card" explicitly
  (Inferno Core, On Guard, Chain Lightning, Curse Touch, Purify, Verdant Surge, Drown
  Surge); Frostweaver has no such line, so `frost_armor` there is a flagged judgment
  call, not a quote.
  - Caught before shipping: `CardView.BuildSpellCard` hardcodes its header/footer row
    classes rather than exposing them through `CardViewOptions`, and the base sheet
    defines no layout at all for either — every existing card context supplies its
    own. Without adding `.cs-signature-spell-card .card-header { flex-direction: row;
    }` explicitly, the cost pill and name would have stacked vertically instead of
    sitting side by side.
- **Surface gradient.** One painted top-down sheen on the featured panel
  (`DrawTopSheen`, the same stacked-low-alpha-band technique `MapBackgroundElement`
  uses for its glow pools, since UI Toolkit's USS has no linear/radial-gradient
  background support). Scoped to this one surface rather than the card/stat-container/
  footer surfaces the TODO also named — spreading the same treatment across all four
  blind felt like more risk than the item's value justified.
- **Ambient particles** in the featured panel's otherwise-empty upper zone — 7
  drifting dots tinted to the selected class's colour, reusing the title screen's
  existing `.particle` drift-and-twinkle idiom. Also resolves "elemental aura motion"
  by not adding a third competing layer on top of the ring rotation + glow breathing
  already there, which was the reason that item was deferred in the first place.
- **Dead CSS found, not touched:** `.cs-feat-matchup` / `.cs-matchup-*` in
  `WizardBattle.uss` have no UXML markup or C# builder referencing them anywhere —
  the matchup section (STRONG VS / WEAK TO / BEST FOR) doesn't exist on this screen
  in the current demo. This closes "collapse signature spell row into the matchup
  section" as N/A rather than building a matchup section from scratch just to
  collapse into it.

### Map screen

- **Node-type patterned fill**, extended from Elite/Boss (which already had it) to
  Combat, Shop, Event and Rest: a smaller concentric copy of the same shape stroked
  at 35–50% alpha. Reuses `FillPoly`/`StrokePoly`/`FillCircle`/`StrokeCircle`/
  `StrokeRoundedSquare` already proven safe in `MapNodeElement.DrawShape` rather than
  a new drawing primitive.
- **Density overlay toggle** (⚑ in the map HUD): dims every node except Elite/Boss
  (danger, red), Shop (reward — the only gold-spend node, gold) and Rest (healing,
  green), which gain a matching ring.
  - Caught before shipping: `MapNodeElement` draws its entire shape via `Painter2D`
    and zeroes its own USS border **inline**, in its constructor, so styling
    `.map-node.node-elite { border-width: 3px; }` directly would never have rendered
    — an inline style always wins over USS. The ring is a separate sibling
    `VisualElement` placed next to each qualifying node instead.
- **True scroll-parallax** for the map background, without the restructuring that
  was originally deferred over. `MapBackgroundElement` stays exactly where it already
  was (a normal child of the scrolled canvas); its glow pools and depth layers are
  now painted at `baseY + scrollOffsetY * 0.45` instead of `baseY`, which works out
  to a real 55%-speed parallax on screen. `MapScreen.TickNodes` feeds the current
  scroll offset in every tick (already running at 60fps for node bob), no-op'd below
  a 0.5px threshold. Act bands are deliberately excluded — they're pinned to real
  floor Y positions and parallaxing them would visibly separate the colour band from
  the floor boundary it marks.
- **Node unlock (entrance) animation.** The concern this was originally deferred over
  — two `animation-name` values fighting during a USS-keyframe-to-idle handoff —
  doesn't actually apply here: node motion has never been USS `@keyframes` in this
  project (they don't run at runtime); it's imperative per-frame `style.translate`/
  `style.opacity` writes in `MapScreen.TickNodes`. The entrance is one more term in
  that same formula, converging to a no-op once it finishes, so there's no handoff
  moment for two animations to conflict over. Scoping note: plays on every map
  (re)build for every available node, not gated to a genuinely-first-ever unlock —
  that would need tracking each node's prior availability across screen visits,
  which `BuildAvailableSet` doesn't currently persist, and this pass didn't want to
  add that state-tracking blind for a purely cosmetic gate.
- **Route transition animation**, implemented as a global cross-screen fade in
  `ScreenManager.Show` rather than a change to `GameManager.EnterNode`'s dispatch
  itself — that dispatch is a plain synchronous call every downstream system
  (battle setup, rest/shop/event screens) assumes completes the switch immediately,
  and inserting a delay there risked exactly the gameplay-flow bug this item was
  deferred over needing Play-mode to catch. The fade lands on every screen switch in
  the game uniformly instead of only map travel, and changes no gameplay ordering.

### Compile checks along the way

Two real compile errors surfaced and got fixed before this landed: `ToggleInClassList`
returns `void` in this UI Toolkit version, not `bool` (the overlay toggle button was
written assuming otherwise); and the map's entrance-animation code referenced a `dt`
local that only exists in `ClassSelectScreen.Tick()`, not `MapScreen.TickNodes()`
(they compute their delta-time inline instead). Both caught by the headless EditMode
run before commit, not shipped.

### Validation

- Unity 6000.4.8f1 EditMode suite: **199 passed / 0 failed**, 0 `error CS`.
- **Not verified on device or in Play mode.** Every item above that carries a "Play-
  mode verification" caveat in its original TODO entry still carries one — this pass
  found lower-risk ways to implement the *feature*, not a way to *see* it running.
  The whole batch is queued for the single visual pass at the end of this session,
  same as the earlier narrow-layout fix.

## b16 · 2026-09-08 — Fix title screen overflow at large UI sizes

### Bug Fix — Home screen didn't compensate for the UI size setting
- Reported after build 15 shipped: at UI size 115%/130%, the title screen's hero content ran
  off the bottom of the phone rather than compacting to fit.
- **Root cause, worked out from the panel-scaling math rather than guessed at.** UI size
  shrinks the logical viewport (panel scaling with match 0.5 takes the geometric mean of the
  axis ratios), so an iPhone 17 Pro that measures ~977 logical px wide at 100% drops to ~849
  at 115% and ~751 at 130%. Two things break at that width and they compound: the hero block
  (`title-logo`, the element tiles) is sized in fixed pixels with `flex-shrink: 0`, so it has
  no way to give height back, and the element grid — four tiles per row down to 849px — drops
  to three per row and *gains* a whole row of height at the exact moment height gets scarcest.
  At 130% the hero needed roughly 1940px in a 1634px viewport.
- **Fix:** a new `layout-narrow` breakpoint (`ResponsiveLayout.IsNarrow`, <900 logical px —
  reachable only via the UI size setting; no supported device hits it at 100%) plus a
  title-screen USS block sized for the 130% worst case: logo 440×568, element tiles
  160×215 with tighter margins so they **stay four across at 751px** rather than wrapping to
  three, and trimmed CTA button heights. Brings the hero to ~1330px with real slack to spare;
  115% shares the same block and reads a little airy rather than cramped, which is the right
  side to err on.
- Deliberately placed after the existing `layout-tall-phone` rules in `WizardBattle.uss`: both
  selectors carry identical specificity, so `layout-narrow` only wins by sitting later in the
  cascade. Commented in place so a future edit doesn't reorder it by accident.
- Only the title screen was in scope for this pass — it's the screen that was reported broken.
  Other screens have not been checked at 115%/130% and may have the same fixed-pixel-hero
  problem; worth a look before calling the UI size setting fully verified.

### Tests
- Four new cases in `AccessibilitySettingsTests`, converting the panel-scaling arithmetic into
  an assertion rather than leaving it as a comment: `ScalingTheUiShrinksTheLogicalViewport`,
  `ScalingNeverChangesTheAspectDrivenBreakpoints` (aspect is invariant under uniform scaling,
  so a phone must stay `layout-tall-phone` at every step — only the width/height *threshold*
  classes may move), and `EnlargedUiTripsTheNarrowLayoutButDefaultDoesNot`, which is the
  regression test proper: 100% must stay off `layout-narrow`, 115% and 130% must trip it,
  measured against a real iPhone 17 Pro logical size rather than an arbitrary number.

### Validation
- Unity 6000.4.8f1 EditMode suite: **199 passed / 0 failed** (196 before), 0 `error CS`.
- Not yet re-verified on device — the original report came from the phone, this fix was built
  and tested from the panel-scaling math. Worth a follow-up screenshot at 130% before treating
  this as fully closed.

## b16 · 2026-09-06 — Accessibility settings: UI size and a colourblind-safe palette

Closes the last two items on `TODO-map-uxui.md`'s and `docs/wizard-select-todo.md`'s
accessibility lists that did not need a device or a human in the room.

### New Feature — Settings → UI size
- A four-step ladder (Small 90% / Default 100% / Large 115% / Largest 130%) on the title
  screen's existing settings panel, persisted as `settings.uiScale`.
- Implemented by dividing `PanelSettings.referenceResolution` down from a constant
  1080×1920 base: fewer logical pixels across the same physical screen means every px in USS
  covers more of it. `AccessibilitySettings.ReferenceResolutionFor` always recomputes from
  that constant rather than from the asset's current value — deriving it from the live value
  would compound on every apply. The asset is only written when the value actually differs,
  so a player who never opens the setting can't end up with a dirtied `PanelSettings.asset`.
- **Interacts with `ResponsiveLayout` by design.** Aspect ratio is invariant under uniform
  scaling, so the `layout-portrait`/`layout-tall-phone` classes never move. The two absolute
  thresholds do: `DesktopMinWidth` (1000) and `ShortLayoutMaxHeight` (820) are logical
  pixels, so at 130% a 1920×1080 window measures 1477×831 logical and picks up
  `layout-short`. That is the correct response to genuinely having less vertical room, not a
  regression — but it does mean each step is a layout configuration, which is why this is a
  four-stop ladder and not a slider.

### New Feature — Settings → Colour palette → "Colourblind-safe"
- Recolours the eight elements, plus the four red/green semantic tokens, to a palette whose
  members stay apart under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. Persisted as
  `settings.colorVision`; default is unchanged.
- **The problem, measured.** Simulating each deficiency (Viénot/Brettel/Mollon) and
  measuring CIEDE2000 distance between every pair of element colours:

  | | shipped palette | colourblind-safe |
  |---|---|---|
  | closest element pair, worst case | **dE 1.3** (Fire/Arc, tritanopia) | dE 11.6 (Rock/Shadow) |
  | Fire/Arc under deuteranopia | dE 4.1 | dE 28.2 |
  | `--success` vs `--danger-soft` under deuteranopia | **dE 3.3** | dE 39.5 |
  | `--hp-player` vs `--hp-enemy` under deuteranopia | dE 8.3 | dE 44.3 |

  The `--success`/`--danger-soft` number is the one worth flagging: those are the STRONG VS /
  WEAK TO rows on class select and the "Super effective!" / "Not very effective..." badges
  added to hand cards on 2026-08-17. At dE 3.3 a deuteranope reads those two as the same
  colour — the text carries all of the meaning. Cyan/amber in place of green/red fixes it.
- The alternative palette also lifts Shadow off a **2.23:1** contrast floor against
  `--surface-1`, which was below the 3:1 non-text minimum even for normal colour vision.
- Enemy-card name and type labels take one tint per element in this mode rather than the base
  sheet's pale-name/saturated-type split: at these lightnesses the saturated versions
  reconverge (Water/Plant fall to dE 2.7) and several drop under 4.5:1 against their own
  header. One tint holds every label at ≥4.5:1 and ≥dE 8.1 apart; name-vs-type hierarchy is
  carried by the size and weight already in the base sheet.

### Refactor — one source of truth for element colour
- New `TypePalette` (`Assets/Scripts/UI/TypePalette.cs`) holds both palettes and resolves
  against the current setting. It replaces **three** separate copies of the same nine
  colours: identical `TypeColors` dictionaries in `CardView.cs` and `BattleScreen.cs`, and
  the per-class hex literals in `ClassSelectScreen.cs`'s `ClassDef` table (`ClassDef.Color`
  is now `TypePalette.Hex(Element)`). All three already agreed; the point is that they no
  longer *can* disagree, and that the colourblind option reaches all of them at once.
- USS side: `Assets/Resources/Styles/ColorblindPalette.uss` restates only the colour-bearing
  declarations, with the base sheet's alpha values preserved exactly — silhouette shapes,
  sizes and rotations stay in the base sheet, so changing one needs no edit here.
- `AccessibilitySettings.ApplyTo` is called from `ScreenManager.Show`, the one place every
  screen passes through. It has to run on every show, not once: a screen re-clones its UXML
  on enable, which resets `styleSheets`. The override sheet lands on the same element the
  UXML `<Style>` does, so it wins the cascade by being added last, with no specificity games.

### Tests
- New `AccessibilitySettingsTests` (15 cases). Most are ordinary — scale snapping, label
  round-trips, PlayerPrefs defaults, the two new dropdowns existing in the UXML — but three
  are worth naming:
  - `ColourblindPaletteSeparatesEveryElementUnderDichromacy` re-implements the
    Viénot/Brettel/Mollon simulation and re-derives the minimum separation, so a later colour
    tweak that quietly breaks the property fails here instead of shipping.
  - `ColourblindStyleSheetUsesTheSameColoursAsTypePalette` compares the USS rgb triples
    against `TypePalette`, which is the drift this two-copies-of-one-palette design invites.
  - `ScalingAlwaysRecomputesFromTheBaseResolution` guards the compounding bug directly.
- Tests save and restore any pre-existing `settings.*` prefs, so running the suite doesn't
  clobber the developer's own Editor settings.

### Validation
- Unity 6000.4.8f1 EditMode suite: **196 passed / 0 failed** (181 before this change),
  0 `error CS` diagnostics.
- **Not verified on device.** Every claim above is derived from the source and from colour
  maths, not from pixels. Per the standing note in `TODO-map-uxui.md`, the Editor Game view
  has hidden three separate phone-layout bugs before — the 130% step in particular deserves a
  look on a real phone before it ships, since it is the one that can flip a breakpoint.

## b16 · 2026-08-27 — Windows itch.io beta distribution pipeline

### Infrastructure — Third distribution channel (Windows desktop)
- Added `Assets/BuildScripts/upload_to_itch.sh`, the post-build hook for a new **Windows Itch
  Beta** Unity Build Automation target (Windows desktop 64-bit, branch `main`, Unity 6000.4.8f1).
  It pushes the built player to `doctormcboop/wizard-battle-demo:windows` with butler, joining
  `upload_to_testflight.sh` (iOS) and `upload_to_firebase.sh` (Android).
- Versioning is a `date '+%Y.%m.%d.%H%M'` `--userversion` stamp rather than a hand-bumped
  number — unlike TestFlight and Firebase, itch has no duplicate-build-number trap to avoid, so
  there is nothing to remember to increment before a push.
- The script pushes the **directory** containing `$UNITY_PLAYER_PATH`, not the `.exe` alone: a
  Unity Windows player is useless without the sibling `_Data` folder and DLLs. On a Windows build
  agent (`BUILDER_OS = WINDOWS`) the Unity-supplied path is run through `cygpath -wa` first.
- butler is downloaded from `broth.itch.zone` at build time when it isn't already on `PATH`.
  `BUTLER_API_KEY` is set on the build target itself and is not committed.
- Project page (https://doctormcboop.itch.io/wizard-battle-demo) is **Restricted**, not Public —
  testers are invited with generated download keys. Auto-build is off; the target is triggered
  by hand from Configurations, same as the other two.
- Documented in `CLAUDE.md` alongside the iOS and Android pipelines.

## b16 · 2026-08-17 — Battle screen click-affordance fixes

### UX — Unaffordable spell cards no longer invite a dead click
- `WizardBattle.uss`: added `.spell-card.unaffordable:hover`, resetting translate/scale so an
  uncastable card doesn't lift and glow on hover exactly like a castable one — the base
  `.spell-card:hover` rule was firing its full "this is interactive" treatment on cards that had
  no click handler behind them at all.
- `BattleScreen.cs`'s `BuildHandCard`: unaffordable cards now get a real click handler that
  triggers a one-shot `.denied` scale-bounce (new USS class, same idiom as `.enemy-card.hit-flash`)
  instead of silently doing nothing when clicked.

### UX — Type-matchup preview on hand cards
- `BattleScreen.cs`: new `AddMatchupBadge()` shows a hover-reveal "Super effective!" / "Not very
  effective..." pill (new `.card-matchup-badge*` USS classes, reusing the `--success`/
  `--danger-soft` colors from the existing Matchups reference panel) on hand cards once
  `enemy.IsTypeRevealed` is true. Reads `TypeChart.GetMultiplier`/`GetEffectivenessLabel`, which
  previously only fed post-cast damage math and the combat log — the player had no way to preview
  a matchup before spending mana on it. Gated on type-reveal so hovering can't be used to deduce a
  still-hidden enemy type for free (see `BattleEngine.NarrowByEffectiveness`).

## b16 · 2026-08-17 — Focus cost change; spell data generator upsert fix

### Design — Focus now costs 0 mana
- `CreateGameData.cs`'s `CreateSpells()`: Focus (draw 2 cards) mana cost 1 → 0.

### Design — Amplify now reads ×2 in its own spell text
- Updated the "Next spell gains ×1.5 effect." card description to "×2", matching the ×2
  multiplier already in `BattleEngine.cs`/`DuelRulesData.cs`.

### Bug Fix — `S()` in CreateGameData.cs silently no-opped on existing spells
- The spell-asset upsert helper (`S()`) returned early if a `SpellData` asset already existed
  at its path, so editing a spell's cost/description/effects in `CreateGameData.cs` and
  re-running `Wizard Battle → Create Game Data` had no effect on already-generated assets —
  it only ever wrote *new* spells. `focus.asset` and `amplify.asset` were stuck with stale
  `manaCost`/`description` values until this was fixed. `S()` now loads-or-creates and
  overwrites fields in place, matching how `C()` (classes) and `TT()` (tutorials) already
  behaved. Regenerating also refreshed several tier-variant spell assets
  (`flame_shield*`, `static_field*`, `thorn_armor*`, `guard`, `mana_petal`) whose serialized
  data had drifted from the generator source.

## b13 · 2026-08-16 — Tutorial shipped on, UI sizing fixes, map re-measure

### Feature flag — Tutorial is now ON
- `FeatureFlags.TutorialEnabled` flipped to `true`, so the TUTORIAL button ships to playtesters.
  Build numbers bumped to **13** (iPhone + Android) for the TestFlight/Firebase upload.

### Design — TUTORIAL promoted to its own title-screen button
- Moved the entry point out of the utility row (HOW TO PLAY/TYPES/HISTORY) into a full-width
  `btn-tutorial-title` CTA of its own, below the ADVENTURE/DUEL row rather than folded into that
  row's hand-tuned 62/38 split — deliberately avoids touching that split's width math across the
  desktop/short/tall-phone variants. Styled to match `btn-duel-title` (dark surface, gold border,
  Cinzel-Bold), with responsive overrides mirrored from it at each breakpoint.

### Design — Tutorial Tower screen and callouts enlarged
- The intro/tower/outro screen and the in-battle callout were both sized for a desktop-ish
  viewport and read as tiny on a real phone. Bumped the tower's type, node circles, numbers and
  labels, and added a `layout-tall-phone` step-up on top of that.
- The callout popup originally tried to hug whichever element it pointed at, computing left/top
  from the target's `worldBound`; this put it in awkward places and sized it inconsistently across
  aspect ratios. It now docks to a fixed, flex-centered position (86% width, capped 640px) and
  only the gold highlight ring still tracks the target's bounds — degrading to hiding itself if
  those bounds aren't ready, rather than mis-placing the whole popup.

### Bug Fix — Tall-phone hand now wraps to two rows
- The hand was tuned so exactly five cards fit one row without scrolling, which forced a ~172px
  card floor that proved too cramped to read on device. Widening cards within one row is *not* a
  fix: the hand `ScrollView` is in UI Toolkit's default **vertical** mode, so an over-wide row
  does not scroll horizontally — the overflowing card is silently clipped and unreachable. (An
  interim 236px single-row attempt in this session did exactly that to the 5th card.)
- The hand now wraps to **two rows of three**. Each card gets ~296px — wider than either previous
  attempt — so descriptions wrap less and cards can be shorter in exchange, paying for the second
  row. Degrades correctly for variable hand sizes: six fill two rows, seven+ spill to a third and
  scroll *vertically*, which this ScrollView does support.
- Note for future edits: `BattleScreen.RenderHand` sets `flex-direction`, `align-items` and both
  paddings on the content container **inline**, which beats USS — a pre-existing tall-phone rule
  setting padding there had never taken effect. The wrap rule sets only `flex-wrap`/
  `align-content`/`justify-content`, none of which are assigned inline.

### Bug Fix — Map screen scrolled on notched phones
- The map canvas is sized to fit the viewport *exactly* (`BuildMap`'s row-height maths solve so
  `canvasH == h` whenever the fitted row height clears `MinRowHeight`), so it should not scroll on
  a phone at all. It did on iPhone, because the map built **once**, on the first non-zero
  `GeometryChangedEvent`, and latched via `_built` forever. `SafeAreaPadding` applies its notch
  inset *after* that first measurement, so the canvas kept the taller pre-inset height while the
  viewport shrank beneath it. Never reproduced in the Editor, where `Screen.safeArea` is the whole
  screen and no late inset arrives.
- `MapScreen` now re-measures and rebuilds whenever the viewport size actually changes (0.5px
  epsilon guard against float jitter, so it cannot loop). `StartNodeAnimation` was already
  rebuild-safe. Fixed alongside: the geometry callback was registered on every `OnEnable` and
  never removed, so handlers stacked across map visits — now unregistered in `OnDisable`.
- If a device still scrolls after this, the remaining lever is `MinRowHeight` (110px on mobile,
  deliberately "scroll rather than squish"), which forces an oversized canvas on short viewports.

### Bug Fix — Tutorial tests were coupled to the feature flag
- `TutorialManagerTests` passed only because `TutorialEnabled` was `false`, which made
  `ScreenManager.ShowTutorial()` an early-return no-op; switching the tutorial on turned all 9
  into `NullReferenceException`s inside `ScreenManager.Show(null)`. The fixture now injects a
  stand-in `TutorialScreen` into the private serialized field, so it exercises the real path and
  no longer depends on a shipping flag's value.

## 2026-11-01 — Internal version 0.1.2

### Docs

- **The game's version is now 0.1.2, kept in `VERSION` at the repo root.** It is an internal
  label only: nothing in the build reads it. The store-facing `bundleVersion` stays 2.0.0,
  because App Store Connect appears to have an approved 1.0 (unconfirmed) and would reject uploads with a lower version.
  `tools/tag-release.sh` prints it and puts it in the tag message.

## 2026-11-01 — No testers: drop the tester framing

### Docs

- **CLAUDE.md, README and `deploy-firebase.sh` no longer describe a tester channel.** There are
  no testers; TestFlight, Firebase and itch.io builds only reach the developer's own devices.
  The README also stops claiming Online PvP is playable (Duel mode is switched off).
- `tools/tag-release.sh` and the changelog stamping are now optional after a build. Build numbers
  from git stay, since they stop App Store Connect rejecting duplicate build numbers.

- `tools/export-release-data.sh` was briefly removed (`a24ed2f`) and then restored: the
  wizardbattle.jaredluyster.com/releases/ page it feeds is live and also tracks todos.

## 2026-11-01 — Run the simulator build from Xcode

### Tooling

- **`./run-ios-sim.sh --xcode`** exports the simulator project (`Builds/iOS-Simulator`) from the
  current checkout and opens `Unity-iPhone.xcodeproj` in Xcode instead of building headless:
  pick a simulator and press Run for the Xcode debugger, console and Instruments. Same settings
  revert as the headless path. Xcode's simulator build signs ad hoc, so no team or certificate
  setup is needed. Re-run after code changes; the export overwrites the project.

## 2026-11-01 — Release tracking: build numbers from git, tags, stamped changelog

### Tooling

- **Build numbers now come from git.** New Unity Build Automation pre-export method
  `CloudBuildVersioning.SetBuildNumbersFromGit` (`Assets/Editor/CloudBuildVersioning.cs`) sets
  iOS `buildNumber` and Android `versionCode` to `git rev-list --count HEAD` for the built commit,
  in memory for that build only, so there are no more bump commits. It fails the build instead of
  guessing: a shallow clone it can't unshallow, a count at or below the last hand-bumped build
  (16), or no git. It logs `DuelModeEnabled` / `TutorialEnabled` and warns when duel is on.
  **Not active until the pre-export method is set on the iOS and Android targets in the dashboard.**
- **Windows itch.io builds are versioned `bN`** with the same number (`upload_to_itch.sh`),
  falling back to the old timestamp when the builder has no full git history.
- **`tools/tag-release.sh <commit>`** tags the built commit `bN` and stamps the changelog entries
  that commit contains. `--stamp <tag>` stamps for an existing tag.
- **`tools/export-release-data.sh [path]`** writes `releases.json` for
  wizardbattle.jaredluyster.com/releases/: one release per tag (date, sha, `bundleVersion`, both
  flags, stamped changelog), plus unreleased commits and changelog, the build number HEAD would
  get, and clean/pushed state. It refuses to write output containing an email, a UUID-style id or
  a key-shaped string, since the site is public.

### Changelog

- Stamped the existing tags: 2 entries `b13` (the 2026-08-16 Android 1.2.0 build) and 10
  entries `b16` (2026-08-17 to 2026-09-08, the current TestFlight build). Both builds have PvP on.

## 2026-10-30 — Class-select names clipped on phones

### Bug Fix

- **Class names on the Choose Your Class grid rendered as a sliver of their top edge** on the
  iPhone 17 Pro simulator (tall-phone portrait). `.cs-card-name` carried `overflow: hidden` +
  `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and the portrait override now sets `overflow: visible` /
  `text-overflow: clip` (`WizardBattle.uss`). All eight names, including Verdantmaker and

- **Symbols rendered as empty boxes on device** (`✦ ✕ ☠`, plus `⚔ ⚙ ⚑`). Inter has none of them.

## 2026-10-19 (later) — Affordance Phase 1: events and the rest site explain themselves

### New Feature

### Design Doc

- **New `TODO-affordance.md`**, a phased plan from a screen-by-screen affordance review. The main

## 2026-09-22 — Hand cards beyond the first screenful were completely unreachable

### Bug Fix

- **The battle hand (and duel hand) can now actually be scrolled to reach every card.**
  `HandSize` is 5 (`BattleEngine.cs`) and hand cards don't shrink, so a full hand routinely
  overflows one row — reported as "can't see full hand" with only 3 of 5 cards visible, and the
  scroller was hidden by design, so there was no visible way to reach the rest. Two compounding
  bugs, found by decompiling `UnityEngine.UIElementsModule.dll` after CSS fixes alone didn't move
  the needle: (1) neither hand `ScrollView` ever set `mode`, so it defaulted to `Vertical` and never
  scrolled a row that overflows *sideways* — now set explicitly in code (`BattleScreen.cs`,

  tall-phone card grid, which wraps into rows and needs the opposite axis. (2) `ScrollView`'s

## 2026-09-21 (later) — The enemy readout moves inside the card (critique 3.1, 1.3)

Phase 3 of `TODO-battle-ui-critique.md`, the last structural item. Closes 1.3 along with it, which
the plan had predicted would come free here.

### Design

- **The enemy panel now carries its own numbers.** It was the biggest thing on screen with the
  least information per pixel — a name, a type, a tier and a large mostly-empty picture — while HP,
  statuses and intent floated underneath as three unrelated sibling widgets. All three moved into a
  new `.enemy-card-readout` band inside the card, between the art and the footer.
- **1.3 closed by the same change.** "Does the enemy have a defense, weakness, or special
  condition?" was answerable only by reading the status row and the intent pill as two separate
  widgets. They are one banded panel now, beside the HP bar, inside the card that describes them.

### Refactor

- **The art frame is the card's only flexible child**; header, readout and footer are all
  `flex-shrink: 0`. If the height arithmetic is off anywhere, the picture gives and the silhouette

## 2026-09-20 (later still) — The enemy's turn is visible (critique 1.5)

Closes Phase 1 of `TODO-battle-ui-critique.md` except 1.3, which Phase 3 mostly subsumes.

### New Feature

- **The enemy's turn plays out instead of appearing already finished.** Tapping END TURN used to
  jump straight to the next player turn — HP changed, the log gained lines, and the player never
  saw the enemy act. Now the turn is stepped through: Char/Drown ticks land on the enemy, the
  enemy's action lands on the player with a red flush and a damage float, the log reveals a line at
  a time, and the tactical zone recedes while none of it is actionable.

### Refactor

- **`EndPlayerTurn` returns an ordered `List<BattleEvent>`.** Each entry carries the combatants as
  they stood immediately after that step, plus `logCount` — the log's length at that moment — so
  the UI can step the bars and the log through the turn rather than jump to the settled values.
  - **The engine did not become asynchronous.** It still resolves the whole turn synchronously
    inside `EndPlayerTurn`; it just says what it did on the way out. That keeps `CLAUDE.md`'s
    "battle is a pure state machine" note true, and is why all 222 pre-existing EditMode tests pass
    untouched. All timing lives in three `const float` beats in `BattleScreen`.
  - The record stops where the battle ends, so a lethal hit ends the replay on the killing blow
    rather than on a turn the player never got.

### Bug Fix

- **Damage floats now show HP actually lost, not damage rolled.** Floating a pre-block number over
  a fully blocked hit was a lie; a blocked hit reads as the shield pill dropping instead.

### Tests

- **9 new EditMode tests** (`EnemyTurnEventTests.cs`) covering resolution order, that each snapshot
  is the state at that step and not the settled state, monotonic `logCount` ending at the full log,
  mid-turn battle end, the frozen-out turn and a forced Blind miss. Suite: **231 passing, 0
  failing** (Unity 6000.4.8f1 batchmode).

### Watch out

- **`state.isPlayerTurn` is already `true` while the replay runs**, because the engine resolves
  `StartPlayerTurn` synchronously. It cannot guard END TURN — a `replayingEnemyTurn` flag does, and
  the button is disabled for the duration. Anything later that reads `isPlayerTurn` as "the player
  can act" needs to know this.
- **The replay steps HP, block and the log, but not status badges.** Those would need both status
  dictionaries snapshotted per event; the final `Render()` settles them.

### Not verified

- **Nothing here has been seen running.** In particular the pacing — 0.30s lead-in, 0.34s per step,
  0.48s on an attack, roughly 1.1s for a typical turn — was chosen by reasoning, not by feel, and is
  the single most likely thing to need tuning. Too slow and it drags on every turn for the rest of
  the game.

- **PvP had been shipping to playtesters by accident for a month.**
  `FeatureFlags.DuelModeEnabled` was flipped `false` → `true` in `74acf2c` (2026-08-16) —
  a commit whose subject and body are entirely about turning `TutorialEnabled` on, with no
  mention of duel anywhere. The XML comment above the flag still described it as held back
  for a PvE-only build, and `CLAUDE.md` still documented it as `false`; only the value had
  moved. Every TestFlight and Firebase build since has carried the DUEL button (Online PvP,
  Local Hot-Seat, Duel Lab).
  Restored to `false`, matching the documented intent from `0d2512a` ("Gate PvP out of next
  build"). The gating itself was verified intact first — `TitleScreen.ConfigureDuelEntry`
  hides the button and hands ADVENTURE the full mode row via `mode-actions-solo`, and
  `ScreenManager.ShowDuel` early-returns — so no other change was needed. The history is
  recorded in the flag's own comment so the next reader doesn't have to re-derive it.
  **Testers who found DUEL in the last month will lose it on the next build.**
